entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4975"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 24</title> <div sID="gen7341" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="Job.24.1-Job.24.25">Job 24:1-25</reference>.<div eID="gen7341" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7342" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4975"/>1. Why is it that, seeing that the times of punishment (<reference osisRef="Ezek.30.3">Eze 30:3</reference>; "time" in the same sense) are not hidden from the Almighty, they who know Him (His true worshippers, <reference osisRef="Job.18.21">Job 18:21</reference>) do not see His days (of vengeance; <reference osisRef="Joel.1.15">Joe 1:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Pet.3.10">2Pe 3:10</reference>)? Or, with Umbreit less simply, making the parallel clauses more nicely balanced, Why are not times of punishment hoarded up ("laid up"; <reference osisRef="Job.21.19">Job 21:19</reference>; appointed) by the Almighty? that is, Why are they not so appointed as that man may now see them? as the second clause shows. Job does not doubt that they are appointed: nay, he asserts it (<reference osisRef="Job.21.30">Job 21:30</reference>); what he wishes is that God would let all now see that it is so. <div eID="gen7342" type="x-p"/>
